name: Kṛṣṇa (Vāsudeva)
summary: In BhG 16–18 Kṛṣṇa teaches the divine and demonic endowments, the guṇa-classification of faith, food, sacrifice, austerity, giving, knowledge, action, agent, understanding, steadiness and happiness, the meaning of saṃnyāsa and tyāga, and the course from one's own work to becoming Brahman, supreme devotion and entering him; he speaks of the Lord in the heart of all beings (18.61) and gives the 'most secret word': refuge in him alone, with the promise of release from all sins (18.64–66). Sañjaya calls him the lord of yoga (18.75, 18.78).

name: Arjuna (Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya)
summary: In BhG 16–18 Arjuna asks about those who sacrifice with faith outside scriptural injunction (17.1) and about the truth of renunciation and relinquishment (18.1); told he is born to the divine endowment (16.5) and dearly loved (18.64–65), he declares at the end that his delusion is destroyed, his memory regained by Kṛṣṇa's grace, and that he will do Kṛṣṇa's word (18.73).

name: Sañjaya
summary: Narrator of the Gītā to Dhṛtarāṣṭra; at its close (18.74–78) he says he heard the wondrous, hair-raising dialogue directly from Kṛṣṇa by the grace of Vyāsa, rejoices again and again in recalling it and Hari's form, and holds that where Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna are there are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm right conduct.

name: Vyāsa (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana)
summary: By Vyāsa's grace Sañjaya heard the Gītā directly from Kṛṣṇa (BhG 18.75).

name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
summary: The king ('rājan') to whom Sañjaya addresses the close of the Gītā (18.76–77).
